clue.text: Stimulate desire to vomit violently having dined

indicators.note: violently signals that the letters of vomit are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to have dined is to have eaten, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A grim description of feeling sick straight after a big meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' shuffles VOMIT into MOTIV; ATE (dined) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a motive is to stir up their wish to act, hence stimulate desire.

clue.text: First person holds ditto to be a foreign lady

indicators.note: holds means one word contains the other

parts.note: me is the first person pronoun
ditto means the same again: another first person, the first man in Genesis, Adam

explanation.surface: Someone claims that being the same again makes a lady from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditto' repeats 'First person' in another sense: the first human, ADAM, held inside ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French form of address for a married woman, a lady from abroad.

clue.text: Upset dessert, sparking a riot in the café

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the dessert is written backwards

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dessert

indicators.note: sparking off means setting in motion, so the letters of a riot are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dessert gets knocked over and starts a brawl in the café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses TART to TRAT; 'sparking' rearranges A RIOT into TORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian restaurant, the sort of eatery a café is.

clue.text: Essential figures for the figure-conscious

explanation.surface: Key data for those watching their shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital statistics are key data, and also bust, waist and hip measurements, of interest to those minding their shape.

clue.text: Thing that plays oddly and closely

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something that performs strangely and at close quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightly means close together or firmly packed, so closely.

clue.text: Short-fitting cloak for rub-off

indicators.note: a cloak wraps round something, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: fitting means apt

indicators.note: off as in gone wrong signals that the letters of rub are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailoring note about a short cloak worn so it won't rub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns RUB into BRU, which APT cloaks: A-BRU-PT.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt reply is curt and brief, a short one.

clue.text: Pleads for enquiry that avoids the issue

explanation.surface: A plea for an investigation that dodges the real problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to plead for, and the question is the enquiry; the phrase also means an argument assuming what it should prove, evading the issue.

clue.text: Join ascending retinue topped and tailed

indicators.note: ascending in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
topped and tailed means the first and last letters are cut off

explanation.surface: A procession climbing upwards, trimmed at both ends, comes together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' trims RETINUE to ETINU; 'ascending' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring together or combine, to join.

clue.text: Very old hat in France almost a sin

parts.note: tres is French for very

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: passe is French for out of date, old hat

explanation.surface: A very old hat in France is almost a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' covers both words: French TRÈS (very) and PASSÉ (old hat) less its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is an old word for a wrong or sin, as in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Knight putting God first and woman second

indicators.note: first means the God piece comes at the start of the answer

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for God
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A knight putting God before women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' is not a knight of the realm: Gladys Knight is the American soul singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The soul singer of the Pips is called Gladys Knight, so Knight is her surname.

clue.text: Early version of conscription

explanation.surface: A first draft of a law bringing in national service.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough first text is called a draft, and compulsory call-up into the forces is also called the draft.

clue.text: Explosive backing, say, provided by brown coal

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for say is written backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
lignite is soft brown coal

explanation.surface: A mining note that a blasting charge was supported by coal from the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: EG (for example, 'say') reversed by 'backing' gives GE; 'provided by' joins it to LIGNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a blasting jelly, a high explosive used in mining.

clue.text: One student in altered surroundings is subjected to savagery

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside another word
surroundings names the outer word that encloses them

parts.note: altered means mutated
one is the Roman numeral I
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student far from home in strange surroundings suffers a brutal attack.
explanation.walkthrough: I and L go inside MUTATED: MUT-IL-ATED. L stands for learner, from the L-plate a British learner driver displays.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mutilated is to be maimed or disfigured by violence, the work of savagery.

clue.text: Port that's short of an oaf

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the word an is removed from the port

parts.note: Antwerp is a major Belgian port

explanation.surface: Someone at the docks is called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTWERP without its opening AN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly, foolish person, a clot or dolt.

clue.text: Races into wild orgy in poor condition

indicators.note: into means the races are put inside the other piece
wild signals that the letters of orgy are rearranged

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A rowdy party breaks out among racegoers, and the place is left a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns ORGY into GROY, and 'into' puts TT inside it: GRO-TT-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotty is British slang for shabby, nasty or run-down.

clue.text: Measures reported in barren lands

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the word is the one that sounds the same

parts.note: steps are measures taken to deal with something

explanation.surface: Official measures reported for the wasteland regions.
explanation.walkthrough: STEPS (measures) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppes are vast treeless grassland plains, such as those of Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Official taking note Cromwell

indicators.note: taking means the official takes in the note

parts.note: a proctor is a university official
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An official noting down Cromwell's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Cromwell ruled England as Lord Protector.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell held the title Lord Protector of the Commonwealth.

clue.text: Sailors in the flow needing a fastener

indicators.note: in means the sailors go inside the word for the flow
needing means lacking, so the letter a is taken out of the anchorage name

parts.note: Scapa Flow is the Royal Navy anchorage in Orkney, called simply the Flow
a crew is a ship's sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors caught in the current need something to hold on to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the flow' is Scapa Flow, the Orkney naval anchorage; SCAPA 'needing a' loses an A, leaving SCAP, and 'in' puts CREW inside it: S-CREW-CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-cap is a threaded lid that fastens a bottle or jar shut.

clue.text: Vessel often seen under glass

explanation.surface: A boat glimpsed through glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ship that trades along the shore is a vessel, and a mat placed beneath a drinking tumbler is also so called.

clue.text: Game doesn't begin with such a stroke

indicators.note: doesn't begin means the game loses its first letter

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and balls

explanation.surface: A game won't start with a particular shot.
explanation.walkthrough: CROQUET loses its first letter; 'such a stroke' means a stroke in that game.
explanation.definitionFit: A roquet is the croquet shot of hitting one's ball into another ball.

clue.text: Token revolution taking place

parts.note: a coup is a sudden political overthrow, a revolution
an event that is on is happening, taking place

explanation.surface: A small gesture marks a revolution as it unfolds.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a voucher or ticket exchanged for goods, a kind of token.

clue.text: Campanologist with vision?

parts.note: a bell-ringer is one who chimes; add a letter and that person becomes an imagined monster or fantasy

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer who sees visions.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild fancy or illusion, a vision; the word splits as chime-r plus a.

clue.text: Agitate for hollow footrest

indicators.note: hollow means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a stirrup is a rider's footrest

explanation.surface: Stirring up trouble over a hollow footrest.
explanation.walkthrough: STIRRUP has seven letters; 'hollow' removes the middle one, an R.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up is to provoke or agitate.

clue.text: Length is added to American island

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length
taken as written

explanation.surface: A length is added to an American island's shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: ELL, an old measure of length, with IS 'added to' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Island in New York harbour was the immigration station for the United States.

clue.text: Kipling's cat, say, left to erect US town

indicators.note: to erect means set upright, so in a down clue the town is read upwards

parts.note: Reno is a town in Nevada

explanation.surface: Kipling's cat left town for America.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 'The Cat that Walked by Himself' is a solitary type, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's cat walked by himself, a classic solitary person, a lone wolf.

clue.text: Give up concealing ugly scene, being compliant

indicators.note: concealing means one word hides the other inside itself

parts.note: to give up is to quit

indicators.note: ugly suggests something messed up, so the letters of scene are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone backs down to cover up a nasty scene and keep the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ugly' turns SCENE into ESCEN, and QUIT conceals it: QUI-ESCEN-T. 'being' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiescent means passive and quiet, so going along without resistance, compliant.

clue.text: Crawler to yield about two points of advice

indicators.note: about means the first word is wrapped around the others

parts.note: to yield is to cede
N, north, is one compass point
a tip is a piece of advice
E, east, is the second compass point

explanation.surface: A creep gives way after hearing a couple of points of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: CEDE goes round N, TIP and E, compass points either side of TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A many-legged arthropod is a crawler, crawling creatures being the sense here.

clue.text: Lay to rest, having missed opening of season

indicators.note: missing the opening means the first letter of the season is dropped

parts.note: winter is a season

explanation.surface: A burial was put off because the season had already begun.
explanation.walkthrough: WINTER loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter someone is to bury them, laying the body to rest.

clue.text: Teacher's in luck, returning to local community

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembly is read backwards
in means the teacher goes inside the word for luck

parts.note: hap is an old word for luck or chance
sir is a schoolchild's name for a male teacher; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A teacher has a stroke of good fortune on coming home to the village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's' reads as 'Teacher is': SIR goes in HAP, giving HSIRAP, which 'returning' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the area served by a church, and in Britain also a small local administrative unit.

clue.text: From above, spot artist (at home) and medic (going to work)

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
in means at home
Dr is short for doctor, a medic
op is short for operation, a surgeon going to work

explanation.surface: A painter at home and a doctor heading off to the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop of rain is a spot that falls from the sky.
